newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money nudges up in tighter conditions.
newsitem.headline: German call money nudges up in tighter conditions.

text.p: German call money rates nudged slightly higher on Thursday to trade between 3.05/10 percent as banks stepped up efforts to prop up their unexpectedly low reserve holdings at the Bundesbank.
The bulk of trades was conducted between 3.07/10 percent, up from Wednesday's 3.07/08 percent rates.

"Reserve holdings were much lower than what the market had expected after Wednesday's 2.2 billion mark money market drain by the Bundesbank," a dealer said. Some dealers said another slight tightening in liquidity conditions could be seen in the next sessions, leaving rates to trade sideways or up slightly.
Banks held 38.7 billion marks in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank on Wednesday, down from 42.6 billion marks on Tuesday.
Average holdings for the month stood at 42.3 billion marks, down from 43.2 billion marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.10567 percent on Thursday, compared with 3.10200 percent on Wednesday.
